subject.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics

question: Should this PR keep a CLI-owned, `diagnostics-otel`-specific lifecycle for embedded one-shot and fallback runs, or should that lifecycle be expressed through a generic plugin-service capability first?
rationale: The patch deliberately introduces a named bundled-plugin service exception in core runtime code and changes exit-time behavior for enabled OTel setups; the protected maintainer and human-review labels require a human ownership decision rather than automated resolution.

options.title: Approve the scoped lifecycle
options.body: Confirm that `diagnostics-otel` is the only short-lived push exporter eligible for embedded CLI startup and accept the documented 10-second shutdown bound.

options.title: Generalize the service seam
options.body: Require a generic plugin-declared one-shot service capability before merging so core does not select a named diagnostics plugin.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped lifecycle
recommendation.body: Confirm that `diagnostics-otel` is the only short-lived push exporter eligible for embedded CLI startup and accept the documented 10-second shutdown bound.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current implementation and most directly can explain the intended service boundary to the reviewing owner.
